segment.description: Duck River below Normandy Dam (Normandy tailwater), Bedford County
segment.boundaries: Normandy Dam downstream through the stocked tailwater reach (TWRA: Normandy Dam to Hall's Mill swift/rocky trout water); USGS 03597860 (Duck River at Shelbyville) is well BELOW this reach and was not used for tailwater conditions

coldSource.notes: TVA includes the Normandy tailwater in its cold-water trout program, but the TWRA-commissioned creel study found dam discharges EXCEED the 22 C downstream temperature target every summer, and September-October 2000 dam-area temperatures were 'the highest recorded in any Tennessee tailwater managed for trout' (Bettoli 2001, TWRA Fisheries Report 01-43, https://duckriveragency.org/_assets_/plugins/Annotated%20Bibliography/NormandyTW2000CreelSurvey.pdf).

holdover.detail: TWRA electrofishing in 1998 found FEW rainbow trout hold over from one season to the next, attributed to elevated late-summer/fall water temperatures (Bettoli 2001, TWRA Fisheries Report 01-43). The same report states stocking in late summer when temperatures routinely exceed 25 C 'is clearly a waste of resources'.

wildPopulation.detail: No natural-reproduction data found for this tailwater in the creel report or elsewhere in this pass; unknown.

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: TWRA's own commissioned study measured 27 C (acutely lethal to rainbow trout) below Normandy Dam in late August 2000 and found few stocked trout survive summer - consistent with TWRA's current winter-months stocking pattern (Jan, Feb, Mar, Nov, Dec rainbow per the owner-supplied 2026-09-17 TWRA workbook).
